summary: Request: advice and safe revert playbook for combined batching/caching/quantization tuning causing intermittent 5xx and output regressions
description: Customer ScaleOps enabled an aggressive Optimize profile (aggressive_batching=true, kv_prefix_cache=enabled, quant_profile=custom-low-bit) across several Dedicated pools to cut per-token cost. After rollout to production traffic at 2026-03-09T22:30Z they report intermittent 5xx spikes, elevated tail latency for streaming responses, and subtle semantic output degradation on long-context prompts. They want guidance on tuning knobs (batch size, cache TTL, quant profile) and a conservative rollback/playbook that won't cause a second outage.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Send concurrent streaming requests with ~1.5s inter-request arrival and ~1024 token prompts against redwood-7b-v2 in prod/us-east.
2) Observe a subset of requests receiving 502/503 during high QPS (~120 RPS sustained) while average latency remains acceptable.
3) Re-run with Optimize profile disabled and note successful completion and lower tail latency.
4) Validate that requests with long prefixes show lower factuality scores vs baseline when quant_profile=custom-low-bit is active.
observed_behavior: Intermittent 5xx responses (502/503) during sustained high throughput, spike in 99th percentile response time for streaming sessions (from 480ms -> 1.9s), and slight increase in hallucination rate for prompts >800 tokens after enabling custom quant profile.
expected_behavior: Stable throughput with low tail latency and no measurable degradation in generation quality after optimization changes, or a controlled degraded mode with clear rollback path.

investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: aggressive continuous batching + prefix KV caching increases memory pressure on a small subset of GPU nodes, causing RPC failures which manifest as 502/503. The custom quant profile may be increasing per-layer CPU fallback for specific token lengths, contributing to tail latency and quality shifts.
Checked Dedicated pool autoscaler logs: no autoscale events at time of spike; GPU utilization on affected nodes was 78-94% with memory fragmentation observed in metrics.
Batcher metrics show frequent target_batch_size oversubscription during burst windows; sample windows with 92 pending requests indicate batching queue backlog.
Quality regression: micro-eval against the customer's prompt set shows ROUGE dropped 2.6 points when custom-low-bit quant profile active vs baseline fp16 profile for long-context prompts.
proposed_workaround: 1) Immediately reduce continuous batching target size from 64 -> 32 for affected pools via Console (Route: Dedicated Pools -> pool-id -> Optimization -> batching).
2) Temporarily disable prefix KV caching for the redwood-7b-v2 route (Console flag: kv_prefix_cache=false) to reduce memory churn.
3) Revert quant_profile from custom-low-bit -> redwood-default-fp16 for routes serving long-context prompts until further tuning completes.
4) If immediate rollback is risky, apply canary: change settings on 10% of traffic first and monitor for 15 minutes before wider rollout.
5) Open a node-level remediation: restart affected serving nodes that show memory fragmentation (coordinate with SRE).
rollback_playbook: Purpose: safely revert aggressive optimizations with minimal user-facing disruption.
Pre-rollback checks: confirm current stable baseline profile name (redwood-default-fp16), identify pool IDs and route IDs affected, capture current metrics and traces for postmortem.

Step A - Safe revert of quantization:
  a) In Console -> Models -> redwood-7b-v2, set quant_profile to redwood-default-fp16 for the specific route.
  b) Use gradual rollout: 10% -> 50% -> 100%, wait 10 minutes and observe 95/99p latency and 5xx rate at each step.

Step B - Disable prefix KV cache:
  a) Console toggle kv_prefix_cache=false for the route.
  b) Validate memory utilization stabilizes and no OOM traces appear within 5 minutes.

Step C - Reduce batching aggression:
  a) Set continuous_batch_target=32 and max_batch_wait_ms=30.
  b) If tail latency still high, reduce target to 16 temporarily.
  c) Monitor batcher_pending_count and end-to-end 99p latency.
Step D - Node remediation (if persistent): restart 1 node at a time in the affected pool; wait for healthcheck pass before proceeding to next node.
Rollback testing: run customer's representative prompt set against canary route and compare tokens generated to baseline to confirm quality restored.
Communication: notify customer via ticket updates and Slack #support, include expected timeline and whether a short degrade window is expected during canary shifts.
